claims.nodeLabel: Peruvian Air Force anomalous aerial phenomena office (OIFAA / DIFAA)
claims.sourceText: Agencia Peruana de Noticias Andina (Editora Perú), 18 October 2013
claims.text: The office is named Departamento de Investigación de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (DIFAA) and sits under the Dirección de Intereses Aéreos Espaciales (DINAE) of the Fuerza Aérea del Perú. Its reopening and a public reporting channel were announced on 18 October 2013 by the head of DINAE, Coronel FAP Julio Vucetich Abanto, who said the service was acting on an increase in sightings being reported to the media: 'Nos interesa que la población que observa fenómenos aparentemente no convencionales, que le causan extrañeza o preocupación, conozca que existe una institución que hará un adecuado estudio e investigación de su información para darles una respuesta. Esto no ocurría antes.'

claims.nodeLabel: Peruvian Air Force anomalous aerial phenomena office (OIFAA / DIFAA)
claims.sourceText: Agencia Peruana de Noticias Andina (Editora Perú), 18 October 2013
claims.text: DIFAA had been closed for five years before the 2013 reopening, 'a causa de problemas administrativos'. The reopening was announced at an FAP-organised 'Encuentro sobre Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos' addressed to the Nazca Lines question, at which the invited archaeologist Manuel Aguirre Morales said there is no evidence linking the Nazca lines to UFOs or extraterrestrial presence.

b.label: CEFAA / SEFAA - Chilean anomalous aerial phenomena office, Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil

edges.label: COMPARISON: a military-hosted office against a civil-aviation-hosted one, in the same region
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no joint work is claimed. Andina names Chile among the regional peers DIFAA's reopening brought Peru level with, and reports Peru's stated posture on cooperation as reserved: it considered itself able to analyse the phenomena independently and would appeal to exchange with neighbours only exceptionally, to compare data. Structurally the two are opposites: DIFAA sits inside the Fuerza Aérea del Perú under DINAE, while CEFAA/SEFAA sits inside Chile's civil aviation authority, the DGAC, and frames the subject as an aviation-safety matter. Tier 2 — the structural contrast is analytic, the Peruvian facts are Andina-sourced and the Chilean facts sit on the cefaa and dgac-chile nodes.

b.label: Força Aérea Brasileira / Ministério da Aeronáutica

edges.label: COMPARISON: Peru's own state news agency measured DIFAA's reopening against Brazil
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no institutional contact between the FAP and the FAB is claimed. Peru's state news agency Andina, reporting the reopening on 18 October 2013, closes: 'Con la reapertura de la DIFAA, el Perú se coloca a la paridad de países de la región como Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Brasil y Ecuador.' Brazil is named by a Peruvian government outlet as the regional benchmark. The same report establishes the office's identity that the peru-uap-office node lacked: the Departamento de Investigación de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (DIFAA), sitting under the Dirección de Intereses Aéreos Espaciales (DINAE), whose head Coronel FAP Julio Vucetich Abanto announced the public reporting channel, the office having been closed for five years 'a causa de problemas administrativos'. The reopening was announced at an FAP-hosted 'Encuentro sobre Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos' addressing the Nazca Lines question.

a.label: Peruvian Air Force anomalous aerial phenomena office (OIFAA / DIFAA)

b.label: GEIPAN - Groupe d'Études et d'Informations sur les Phénomènes Aérospatiaux Non identifiés

edges.label: COMPARISON: the military-host model against the space-agency-host model
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no contact is claimed and none was found. DIFAA is hosted by an air force; GEIPAN is hosted by a civil space agency and publishes its case database. The pairing exists on this board to keep the national-office row honest: 'a country has an office' is not one fact but at least three different institutional arrangements, and Peru is the least documented of them. This pass did not locate DIFAA's founding legal instrument, its current reporting line, its case output, or any evidence that it publishes findings.
